children: Bank of America clients were net buyers of U.S. equities
for the second consecutive week last week, driving the biggest inflows since mid-July and the sixth-largest in the firm's weekly data history dating back to 2008.
The massive inflows, totaling $3.9B in single stocks and $3.1B in equity exchange-traded funds, occurred during a week when the S&P 500 (
) rose 0.1%. This momentum was largely fueled by institutional and hedge fund clients, while private clients remained net sellers for a sixth consecutive week. Overall, clients purchased large-
equities but sold off small caps
Under the surface, a clear sector rotation was visible as clients bought stocks in eight of the 11 sectors, led by technology
for the second consecutive week. Tech’s rolling four-week average flows have now been positive since mid-July, and communication services
stocks also experienced inflows for the first time in five weeks.

suffered their fifth consecutive week of outflows, which were the largest of any sector. BofA noted that the rolling four-week average flows for industrials hit record negative levels in the prior week, as positioning began to retreat from highs in what has been considered an expensive and crowded sector. Consumer sectors were the only other groups to experience outflows, reversing the inflows they saw the prior week.
The pivot toward growth was further underscored in the ETF market, where clients bought ETFs across value
, and blend styles. Notably, this marked the first time in five weeks that clients bought growth ETFs. Investors targeted large-, mid- and broad-market-cap ETFs while selling small-cap ETFs.
Sector-wise, clients bought ETFs in seven of the 11 sectors, with health care
leading the pack. In an interesting divergence from the strong single-stock buying in the sector, tech ETFs experienced the largest outflows.

title: BofA clients buy U.S. stocks at 6th-fastest weekly pace since 2008
